stories.headline: AppsFlyer raises over $1B from Google, Meta, Unity and Moloco at $2.7B valuation

key_facts.fact: Ad-measurement firm AppsFlyer raised more than $1 billion in Series E funding at a $2.7 billion post-money valuation, with Moloco, Google, Meta and Unity each acquiring a minority stake.

CEO and co-founder Oren Kaniel said the investments are minority, non-controlling, non-exclusive, and that each investor is integrated with AppsFlyer but will not receive preferential treatment; the transaction is subject to regulatory approvals.
AppsFlyer said it will use the capital to accelerate AI-powered advertising measurement, cross-platform attribution and infrastructure to support autonomous marketing and AI-driven workflows.

The San Francisco-based company works with more than 15,000 brands, has about 1,300 employees, and had previously raised $300 million, including a 2020 General Atlantic-led Series D of $210 million at a $1.6 billion post-money valuation.

stories.headline: Vimeo owner Bending Spoons prices US IPO at up to $1.62B, targeting $19B Nasdaq valuation

key_facts.fact: Italian software company Bending Spoons is seeking to raise as much as $1.62 billion in its US IPO, marketing 58 million shares at $26 to $28 each, for an early-July Nasdaq debut under the ticker BSP.
At the top of the range Bending Spoons would carry a valuation of roughly $19 billion, up from the $11 billion pre-money valuation it achieved when it raised $710 million in late 2025.

Founded in Milan in 2013, Bending Spoons acquires and restructures digital businesses; its portfolio includes Vimeo (acquired for $1.38 billion), WeTransfer, AOL, Eventbrite, Evernote and Komoot, and it reported $27.5 million net income on $601 million revenue for Q1.

About 60% of the IPO shares are primary stock from the company, with the rest sold by existing shareholders including Baillie Gifford; Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan Chase and Allen & Co are leading the offering.

stories.headline: Chevron and Microsoft sign 20-year deal for 2.67 GW gas-powered West Texas data center (Project Kilby)

key_facts.fact: Chevron announced a 20-year power purchase agreement with Microsoft to develop a co-located natural-gas power facility (Project Kilby) supplying dedicated electricity to a Microsoft-operated data center in West Texas.

Project Kilby is expected to deliver approximately 2.67 gigawatts of capacity, consuming roughly the power needed for about two million homes, making it among the largest co-located natural gas power and data center developments in the US.

A majority of the generation will come from large GE Vernova turbines, with additional capacity from Solar Turbines, a Caterpillar subsidiary; the plant will have its own on-site power fueled by Chevron's Permian Basin natural gas in Reeves County.

Chevron expects a final investment decision by the end of 2026 after acquiring necessary permits, with first power delivery anticipated in 2028; Microsoft said the multi-billion-dollar investment over five to seven years would support over 6,000 construction jobs.

stories.headline: China's all-CPU LineShine dethrones El Capitan as world's fastest supercomputer at 2.198 exaflops

key_facts.fact: China's LineShine debuted atop the 67th TOP500 ranking, the first time a China-based system has led since Sunway TaihuLight in 2017, ending El Capitan's run at No. 1.

Installed at the National Supercomputing Centre in Shenzhen, LineShine achieved 2.198 exaflops on the High Performance Linpack benchmark, more than 20% ahead of No. 2 El Capitan, and is the world's fifth exascale system.

LineShine reached the top spot with a domestic CPU-only design built around China's LingKun platform, proprietary LingQi interconnect and Kylin OS, using nearly 14 million cores (LX2 304-core 1.55GHz processors, 13,789,440 total cores).
It is the first supercomputer to officially exceed 2 exaflops on the Linpack benchmark; the announcement was made at the ISC26 conference in Hamburg, Germany.

Experts said the result reflects Beijing's drive for self-sufficiency more than its AI standing: LineShine ranked only fourth on a benchmark designed to simulate AI-like work, and China had stopped submitting systems for three years amid US chip export controls.

stories.headline: Definium's LSD-based DT120 hits primary endpoint in Phase 3 depression trial

key_facts.fact: Definium Therapeutics announced Monday June 22 positive topline results from Emerge, its first Phase 3 trial of DT120 (lysergide, an LSD formulation), a single 100 µg dose in adults with major depressive disorder; the trial met its primary endpoint with a statistically significant improvement versus placebo.

At week 6, the DT120 group showed an LS mean change in MADRS total score of -13.3 versus -5.2 for placebo, an LS mean difference of -8.1 points (p<0.0001); the effect appeared rapid (week 1) and durable (week 12).
The trial involved 149 participants; about 35% of DT120 users substantially responded by week 6 (≥50% reduction) versus 7% of placebo, and 12% reached remission versus 3% of placebo.

Definium is awaiting topline results from a second Phase 3 trial (Ascend) and plans to seek breakthrough therapy designation and expedited approval from the FDA; regulators typically require two positive trials.

stories.headline: FDA reverses course on Regenxbio's Hunter syndrome gene therapy, opens accelerated-approval path

key_facts.fact: Regenxbio announced Monday June 22 that the FDA agreed existing clinical data are sufficient to support an accelerated-approval filing for Navsunli (clemidsogene lanparvovec, RGX-121), a one-time gene therapy for Mucopolysaccharidosis II (Hunter syndrome) — a reversal about four months after a February 2026 rejection.

The FDA confirmed no additional studies are required and that it would not need an untreated control arm it had previously recommended; the company will request a Type A meeting in July and resubmit the BLA in Q3 2026.
The move is part of a broader easing toward rare-disease candidates under new FDA leadership; the prior week the agency made a similar U-turn on uniQure's Huntington's disease gene therapy AMT-130.
Approval of Navsunli could result in a Priority Review Voucher, which Regenxbio retains 100% of the proceeds from; the therapy would be commercialized by Nippon Shinyaku.

stories.headline: Five Eyes cyber agencies warn frontier AI will transform hacking 'in months, not years'

key_facts.fact: On Monday, the cyber security agencies of the US, UK, Canada, Australia and New Zealand issued a rare joint three-page statement warning that frontier AI is rapidly transforming cyber risk and that leaders must act swiftly.

The statement said the timeline for AI-supercharged offensive cyber capabilities 'is not years, it is months,' urging leaders to prioritize foundational security controls and integrate AI into their defenses.

Reuters reported the warning reflects officials' growing concern over models such as Anthropic's Mythos and OpenAI's GPT-5.5-Cyber, said to let users execute complex and potentially devastating hacks.

The statement follows the US government ordering Anthropic to disable a version of Mythos for foreign nationals, and CISA - a co-signer - cutting deadlines for officials to fix serious vulnerabilities to three days, citing AI threats.

stories.headline: Global tech rout: South Korea's Kospi crashes 10%, Nikkei falls 3.5% as AI-chip selloff spreads

key_facts.fact: South Korea's Kospi index closed down 9.99% (910.71 points) at 8,203.84 on Tuesday June 23, its biggest daily plunge since March 4 and the second-largest daily fall of the year; the Korea Exchange triggered a circuit breaker after the index fell more than 8%.

Chip giants Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix each fell more than 12% (12.31% and 12.47%), triggering an automatic 20-minute bourse-wide trading halt; foreign investors were net sellers of roughly 4 trillion won.

The rout spread across Asia: Japan's Nikkei 225 closed down 3.55% at 69,788.38 and Hong Kong's Hang Seng fell about 2%; MSCI's gauge of regional equities declined more than 2% after closing at a record high Monday.
In Europe, the pan-European Stoxx 600 shed 1.2% in early trading with its Technology index down 3.2%; STMicroelectronics and ASMI both fell more than 7%, while Nasdaq 100 futures lost 2.7%.

The selloff followed a tech-led drop on Wall Street Monday where the Nasdaq Composite fell about 1.3% as investors rotated out of 'Magnificent Seven' stocks; a local report said SK Hynix is slowing AI memory chip expansion and shifting to cheaper commodity DRAM.

stories.headline: Groq raises $650M to scale its AI inference cloud after Nvidia licensing deal

key_facts.fact: Groq announced $650 million in new growth capital on Monday, June 22, led by Disruptive and Infinitum, to accelerate expansion of its AI inference cloud.

The raise follows a December 2025 non-exclusive licensing deal with Nvidia, reported at $20 billion, in which Nvidia hired away founder/CEO Jonathan Ross, president Sunny Madra and other staff; investors were paid out and asked to reinvest.
Groq did not disclose its new valuation; it was last valued at $6.9 billion following a $750 million round in September 2025.
The company plans to scale toward 200 MW of inference capacity by the end of 2027, fitting out its footprint with Nvidia's new LPX inference system.

stories.headline: South Korea's KOSPI crashes 9.99% as Samsung and SK Hynix shed over 12%, triggering circuit breaker

key_facts.fact: The KOSPI closed at 8,203.84 on Tuesday June 23, down 910.71 points or 9.99%, its biggest daily plunge since March 4 and the second-largest daily decline of the year.
Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, the market's two largest stocks, slid 12.31% and 12.47% respectively, wiping out billions in market value.

The Korea Exchange activated a circuit breaker on the main board at around 2:33 p.m., halting trading for 20 minutes after the KOSPI fell more than 8% below the previous close; a sell-side sidecar had already been triggered at 11:40 a.m.
The rout followed a tech-led sell-off on Wall Street where the Nasdaq sank more than 1% as Amazon, Nvidia and Microsoft fell sharply, with investors again questioning the AI-fuelled boom.

Analysts attributed the drop largely to profit-taking in semiconductor stocks rather than a macroeconomic deterioration, a day after the index passed the historic 9,100-point level for the first time and the two chipmakers came to make up more than half the market's value.

stories.headline: Nvidia launches Halos for Robotics, a full-stack safety system bringing AV-grade safety to humanoids

key_facts.fact: Nvidia announced Halos for Robotics on June 22, 2026, described as the industry's first full-stack, open robotics safety system that extends Nvidia's autonomous-vehicle safety architecture to humanoids, industrial robots and autonomous mobile robots.

The platform pairs Nvidia IGX Thor hardware and Holoscan Sensor Bridge for AI compute with Halos OS (including Halos Core, a safety OS running Linux and QNX), leveraging over a decade of AV safety R&D, 18,000 engineering years and 21 billion safety transistors.

Agility Robotics is the first to use Halos for Robotics, integrating IGX Thor and Halos Core into the safe human-detection system of its humanoid Digit; Digit will be the first production robot shipping with Nvidia Halos OS, operating in warehouse environments alongside people.

Nvidia also opened the Halos AI Systems Inspection Lab, the world's first ANAB-accredited program for functional and AI safety in both autonomous vehicles and robotics, working with certification bodies including TÜV Rheinland, UL Solutions, TÜV SÜD, exida, SGS and CertX.

stories.headline: OpenAI releases full GPT-5.5-Cyber and launches Patch the Planet with Trail of Bits

key_facts.fact: On Monday, OpenAI expanded its Daybreak cybersecurity program with Patch the Planet, an initiative founded with Trail of Bits (in collaboration with HackerOne and Calif) to help open-source maintainers move from vulnerability findings to deployed fixes.

OpenAI released a full version of GPT-5.5-Cyber, its security-specialized model, scoring 85.6% on the CyberGym benchmark versus 81.8% for standard GPT-5.5; access stays restricted to vetted defenders through its Trusted Access for Cyber program.
More than 30 open-source projects have committed to participate, with initial participants including cURL, Go, Python, Sigstore and pyca/cryptography.

In its first week, Patch the Planet produced hundreds of discovered bugs, 64 pull requests and 51 issues filed across 19 projects, with Trail of Bits putting its entire security research organization on the effort.

OpenAI cited Linux Foundation and Harvard research that 94% of widely used projects studied had fewer than 10 developers responsible for over 90% of code, and said a human security engineer reviews every Patch the Planet finding before it reaches a maintainer.

stories.headline: Oracle says AI adoption helped cut 21,000 jobs in past year, per annual filing

key_facts.fact: In an annual regulatory filing on Monday, June 22, Oracle disclosed its global workforce fell by 21,000 to 141,000 full-time employees as of May 31, 2026, down from 162,000 a year earlier - roughly a 13% cut.
Oracle's filing stated that 'the adoption and deployment of AI technologies across our operations have resulted, and may continue to result, in reductions to our workforce.'
The cuts led to about $1.8 billion in severance and restructuring costs over the past year, up sharply from a $374 million restructuring bill the prior year.

The reductions come as Oracle faces financial pressure from an expensive build-out of AI data centers for customers such as OpenAI and Meta; the company joins peers whose collective AI capex plans could reach $700 billion.

stories.headline: Oracle cut 21,000 jobs in a year, citing AI deployment, as it bankrolls data-center buildout

key_facts.fact: Oracle's global workforce shrank by about 21,000 employees (roughly 13%) in fiscal 2026, falling to 141,000 full-time staff as of May 31, 2026 from about 162,000 a year earlier, according to its annual SEC filing released Monday June 22.
The filing said the 'deployment of AI technologies across our operations have resulted, and may continue to result, in reductions to our workforce.'
The cuts led to about $1.84 billion in severance and restructuring costs in fiscal 2026, significantly higher than the $374 million spent the previous year.

Oracle's capital expenditure for the fiscal year reached about $55.7 billion as it funds an AI data-center buildout for customers including OpenAI; analysts at TD Cowen estimated the workforce reductions would free up roughly $8B-$10B a year in cash flow.

stories.headline: Qualcomm in advanced talks to acquire AI infrastructure startup Modular at ~$4 billion valuation

key_facts.fact: Qualcomm is in advanced talks to acquire Modular Inc. in a transaction valuing the AI infrastructure software company at about $4 billion, per Bloomberg sources, with a deal possibly announced in the coming weeks.
The $4 billion valuation would mark a significant step-up from the $1.6 billion valuation Modular secured in a $250 million funding round just nine months ago, in September 2025.

Modular was founded in 2022 and has raised a total of $380 million to date; Qualcomm is seeking to reduce reliance on the volatile handset market by branching into data center processors and autonomous vehicle chips.

The Modular pursuit follows a separate reported Qualcomm deal to acquire AI chip startup Tenstorrent for $8 billion to $10 billion, which would put combined commitments above $14 billion toward an AI data center ecosystem.

stories.headline: Sakana AI launches Fugu, a multi-agent orchestrator that behaves like a single model

key_facts.fact: Japanese startup Sakana AI publicly released Fugu on Monday, a multi-agent orchestration system delivered as a single foundation model accessible through one OpenAI-compatible API; it ships in two variants, Fugu and Fugu Ultra.

Rather than being a standalone model, Fugu dynamically routes queries to a swappable pool of specialized AI agents, deciding whether to answer directly or assemble and coordinate a team of expert models internally.

Sakana says Fugu Ultra exceeds Claude Fable 5 on LiveCodeBench (Fugu Ultra 93.2, Fugu 92.9, Fable 89.8) and beats Mythos Preview on GPQA-Diamond (Fugu Ultra 95.5, Mythos Preview 94.6), claiming parity with frontier models without export-control exposure.

Sakana frames Fugu as a hedge against vendor lock-in and export controls, noting access to top models 'can disappear overnight' and that orchestrating a swappable agent pool routes around vendor restrictions.
Fugu Ultra went live on Vercel's AI Gateway as 'sakana/fugu-ultra' on Monday, June 22.

stories.headline: SpaceX launches debut $20B+ bond sale, discloses $100.8B cash; stock extends post-IPO slide

key_facts.fact: SpaceX on Monday June 22 announced its first-ever senior unsecured notes offering, targeting at least $20 billion with maturities of five to 30 years, to repay its bridge loan and for general corporate purposes.
SpaceX disclosed it held approximately $100.8 billion in cash and cash equivalents as of June 19, 2026, and received investment-grade ratings: Moody's Baa1, Fitch BBB+, and S&P BBB.

SpaceX stock fell about 16% on Monday in its third straight losing session, having lost nearly 24% over three days, after a record IPO that priced at $135 per share, raised nearly $86 billion (after greenshoe), and made Elon Musk the world's first trillionaire.

Proceeds will help fund SpaceX's AI and data-center buildout, including plans to eventually build data centers in space; the bridge loan accounts for the bulk of SpaceX's roughly $29.1 billion in long-term debt.

stories.headline: SpaceX signs $6.3B compute deal giving Reflection AI access to Nvidia GB300s at Colossus 2

key_facts.fact: SpaceX signed a computing deal with open-source startup Reflection AI granting immediate access to Nvidia GB300 chips at the Colossus 2 data center, with Reflection paying $150 million per month from July 1, 2026 through 2029.
The payments total about $6.3 billion if the agreement runs through the end of its term, though either company can end the contract with 90 days' notice after the first three months.
The Reflection deal is smaller than SpaceX's prior Colossus deals: Anthropic pays about $1.25 billion per month and Google $920 million per month, both also running through July 2029.

Reflection AI, last valued at $25 billion, is building American open-source AI models to compete with OpenAI, Anthropic and Google; the Colossus data center was originally built by xAI, now part of SpaceX, which has turned it into a commercial compute platform.

stories.headline: US and Iran conclude first round of Switzerland talks; US suspends sanctions, releases $12B in frozen funds

key_facts.fact: The first round of high-level US-Iran talks in Buergenstock, Switzerland concluded Monday June 22 after 18 hours of negotiations, with mediators Qatar and Pakistan saying the two sides agreed to a roadmap toward a final deal within 60 days.

The US suspended sanctions against Iran on Monday and, per Iranian state media on Tuesday, Washington agreed to release $12 billion in frozen Iranian funds and temporarily suspend sanctions on Iranian oil.

Treasury Secretary Bessent said Iran committed to free and open transit in the Strait of Hormuz and to permit IAEA inspectors into the country; the Treasury issued a 60-day license allowing Iran to sell previously sanctioned oil.

Vice President JD Vance called the day 'good progress' and said Iran agreed to allow international nuclear inspectors back, calling it a 'major milestone'; Trump posted on Truth Social that Iran would agree to 'Major Weapons Inspections.'

Iran's accounts diverged from the US: Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said only 'a very brief discussion took place regarding the nuclear issue,' and Iran said it intends to maintain control over the Strait of Hormuz and continue charging passage fees.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio was due to start a trip to the UAE, Kuwait and Bahrain to discuss the deal and efforts to secure full and free transit through the Strait of Hormuz.
